name: crypto-retained-oct08-12-features
notes: Original W5 decision/feature/frozen W4 GRU pipeline through fees only. Native inputs separately bounded by opaque-JSON projection before decoding. No new fitting, protected reads or execution.

markets.notes: Settled markets of the two 15-minute series, labelled 1 when YES settled. The vocabularies are params, not code: the five strike types the stage A suite lets through map to a payoff geometry, result is yes or no (void or scalar results are excluded by name, never coerced; this source has no realised settlement value, which source kalshi-history-crypto carries and run-features-hourly.json reads), and the venue spells a settled payload 'finalized'. A market never given a strike (three KXBTC15M rows from 2026-08, 'Target price: TBD') or still unsettled is NOT a row: it lands on the excluded port and the census, by ticker. The 15-minute up/down floor_strike is the window-start target price. strike_known_lag_s: a 15-minute up/down strike is the PREVIOUS market's settlement value (checked on live data: it equals that market's expiration_value) and is published about 7 s after this market opens; the document assumes 30 s, conservative, so a decision is priced only strictly after open + 30 s. A series not listed has its strike at the open. This is the one place the lag is declared; DecisionRows and StrikeAnchors read it from the rows.

markets_through.notes: Drops every market closing at or after W4's end (2026-09-15, W5's start) before anything joins to it: W5 is read by nobody. Earlier markets stay, because a market's strike anchor is the PREVIOUS market's settlement value, so the anchors need the markets before W4 too.

anchors.notes: The up/down series' strikes as observations of the settlement index: each is the index's 60-second average ending at the market's open, in index dollars, known from open + the lag. They are the only index readings in the data, so they anchor the units of the Binance spot (see spot). They are rows of an asset, not of a market: hourly rows can later use the 15-minute series' anchors. A fixed-strike series is not an anchor series. An anchor whose basis is outside the spot node's basis_range is not an observation (a strike in other units).

window.notes: The markets that are decided on: those closing in W4 (2026-08-01 to 2026-09-15, end-exclusive; the upper cut is markets_through). Cut on the CLOSE, as the held-out cut of run-features-15m.json is, so one market has all its leads on one side. 1785542400000 is W2's end, W4's start, pinned by tests/test_w4_take.py.

candles_btc.notes: 1-minute candles of KXBTC15M. The reader converts the candle's END instant from the venue's epoch seconds to the epoch milliseconds every other node uses, and refuses a ts that already looks like milliseconds. One reader per candle source because a snapshot holds one source.

candles.notes: Both assets' candles as one stream. `key: ticker` makes the union refuse a ticker that appears in both ports, which would mean a candle source pulled the wrong series; `provenance` stamps which port each row came from.

fee_schedules.notes: Each series' fee_type and fee_multiplier as the venue reported them at each retrieval. The venue serves only the CURRENT schedule, so a historical market is priced under the latest retrieval; the table says which (fee_schedule_retrieved).

streams.notes: Puts the four Binance streams into the run identity. The feature node reads their daily parquet files itself, which a transform's fingerprint would not cover; this data node (dskit's StreamManifests, ADR-0243) fingerprints each stream's snapshot hash and the feature node refuses a store that moved since. Keys are <ASSET>_<tape> and must match spot.assets (a test pins it).

candles_through.notes: Candles that ended before W4's end only; a decision reads the last candle at or before its instant, so nothing later can matter, and none is passed on.

decisions.notes: One row per market and lead: the INFORMATION instant I = close - lead (decision_ms), at which the spot (the Binance bar that closed before I) and the market quote (the candle that ended by I, the same minute) are read, and the execution instant E = I + exec_lag_s (5 s, a declared latency, must be positive: a fill cannot precede its information), from which the fair-value horizon runs to the close. Reading a quote a minute older than the spot made a simulated zero-edge market look like a 6-standard-error win and a profitable take rule; the zero-edge test pins that it no longer does. The leads are the horizon of the question, a research choice (not a constant of the venue): a 15-minute market is open 15 minutes, so 2, 5 and 10 minutes before the close leave a short, a middle and a long forecast. None may leave less than the 60-second averaging window after E (a test pins it). A lead longer than the market had been open is excluded by name, not clamped. A decision is made only strictly after the strike is known (open + lag): a lead at or above the market's 15 minutes minus the lag is excluded by name (strike_not_known), because there is nothing to price against yet; a test pins the leads below that bound.

spot.notes: Point-in-time spot, basis, log-moneyness ln(K/spot_brti), realised vol and BVOL, strictly before the decision. A 1-minute kline counts only once its close_time_ms is before the decision (bars are labelled by their START, so at 01:00:30 the 01:00 bar is not known); BVOL only if calc_time_ms is strictly before it. Vols are the log-return std per sqrt(second), the square root of dskit's per-bar variance estimators (vol_estimators, ADR-0244) over the bar's seconds, in columns named vol_column_prefix + the estimator's label (rv_rms_60, rv_ewma_30, rv_hl_60): rms = root-mean-square of the last 60 one-minute returns, ewma = half-life 30 bars over the last 300, high_low = Parkinson over 60 bars. A reading older than the age cap is missing (None, flagged), never carried forward; a missing minute blanks the windows it touches. bvol_scale 0.01: the index is published in percentage points (confirmed on a real day in the 2026-10-06 review). UNVERIFIED: seconds_per_year as a 365-day year, and about one BVOL row a second (max_bvol_age_ms assumes it); check one day's file. bar_ms is the interval of the 1m sources (pinned by a test). Klines are USDT-quoted, a proxy for the USD index Kalshi settles on; CC BY-NC-SA, research only. BASIS: strikes are index dollars and the Binance price is on average about 22 USD higher (an unmodelled gap biased every fair value up by about 11 points on live data). For the latest anchor known strictly before the decision (no older than max_basis_age_ms, 20 minutes: longer than the 15 minutes between 15-minute strikes plus the lag) the node divides the anchor by the mean of open and close of the one Binance 1-minute bar before the anchor's window end (it closes 1 ms before the anchor window ends, so it is strictly prior), and multiplies that basis onto the spot: spot_brti. It writes basis, basis_age_ms and basis_missing; no usable anchor means no spot_brti and an unpriced row, never a unit-less price. RANGES: an anchor whose basis (anchor / Binance bar mean) lies outside basis_range is skipped like an anchor with no bar, because the archive holds markets whose floor_strike is the settlement value divided by 10,000 (KXBTC15M-26APR131115-15 reads 7.243729 for 72437.29; five markets of 2026-04-13): taken as an anchor, one prices every later row on a spot of 0.22 to 7.2 with a valid-looking fair value. The basis measured on real days is 0.9989 to 1.0008, so [0.95, 1.05] is wide for the data and narrow for a unit slip; the provenance counts the refused anchors per asset (anchors_out_of_range). max_abs_log_moneyness 1.0: a row whose strike lies further than ln 1.0 from spot_brti (a ratio above 2.7 or below 0.37; the widest real strike, a weekly ladder, was 0.56) is in other units than the index: strike_implausible True, no spot_brti, unpriced and counted (strike_implausible in the provenance); this also covers the bad 15-minute strikes as decision rows. Both knobs are pinned by tests/test_configs.py. The bar mean is a proxy for the 60-second average (1-minute klines hold nothing finer), so each basis carries noise (sd about 14 USD on live data); that, not the level, is what remains. bar_ms and the 60-second averaging window are pinned equal by a test.

state.notes: The market's own YES bid, ask, mid, spread, volume and open interest from the last 1-minute candle that ended at or before the information instant I (the venue's end_period_ts is the inclusive last second of its minute: the candle ending at I covers the same minute as the spot bar, and its close is the last quote in it, so spot and quote carry ONE information instant). A candle that ends after I, and above all after the close (settled prices are about 0 or 1), is never read, and an order fills only at I + the execution lag. A candle older than two minutes is missing, not carried. two_sided means a real, uncrossed bid and ask strictly inside (0, 1): the scorer's gate. Never imputed.

fair_rms.notes: P(YES) under a driftless lognormal with the 60-minute-window realised vol, over the time left, with the settlement-average adjustment: the CF Benchmarks index averages its last 60 seconds, which cuts the variance by 2/3 of that window's point variance (derivation in dskit.pipeline.binary_pricing, ADR-0246). The node prices the horizon from the fill, tau = close - (decision_ms + exec_lag_s), so exec_lag_s here is the SAME 5 seconds as decisions.exec_lag_s (a test pins it; the table's tau_s column and this node's fair_rms_tau must agree). The baseline of the kill test: nothing is fitted. spot_field is spot_brti: the Binance spot in the strikes' units (index dollars), never the raw Binance price.

fair_ewma.notes: The same fair value on the EWMA vol (half-life 30 minutes): a faster-reacting realised vol. exec_lag_s repeats decisions.exec_lag_s (pinned).

fair_bvol.notes: The same fair value on Binance's BVOL implied vol: the market-implied alternative to the two realised vols. Its 30-day tenor is far from a 15-minute horizon, so expect it to be biased, which is the question. exec_lag_s repeats decisions.exec_lag_s (pinned).

fair_gru.notes: P(YES) from the frozen GRU's predictive CDF: the panel row of the decision minute (the bar that closed just before decision_ms, hence row_offset_ms -1), the label horizon of the lead (2, 5 or 10 minutes: an exact panel horizon, rule `nearest`), and 1 - F(ln(strike / spot_brti) / scale) with the panel's own per-row scale. The reference is spot_brti, the Binance spot restated in index units, so the index-Binance basis is carried; the model itself only knows Binance. `panel`: the W4 build (configs/run-panel-build-w4.json), read by source, never by path; `root` is the store. `artifact`: the model saved by the W3 refit (configs/production-args-w4.json), a path relative to the child root, under the git-ignored pipeline_runs/ (the production pipeline's own output; the same convention the zoo and HPO read their results by). `state_hash` pins the exact model into this document's identity (a placeholder until the refit has run; the node refuses a mismatch). group_codes are the panel's asset codes (BTC 0, ETH 1: the order of run-panel-build.json's assets, pinned by a test). `device` is the one the refit recorded; add "device": "cpu" to serve it without a GPU. Rows the model cannot price carry fair_gru null and a status; they are scored as no_forecast, never as a fair value.

fees.notes: Kalshi's taker fee per contract for buying YES at the ask and NO at 1 - bid: the fee of a 100-contract order, rounded up to the cent, divided by 100. The type and multiplier come from the stream. fee_types is the whole Kalshi mapping, in this document and not in any code: Kalshi's `quadratic` type has base rate 0.07 (its published coefficient; rate = 0.07 x multiplier) and is priced by dskit's venue-neutral probability_quadratic mechanic (rate x C x P x (1 - P) for an order of C contracts at price P), rounded UP to the next cent per order (ceil_to_tick, tick 0.01). `contracts` is 1: the test trades ONE contract, so the per-order rounding is paid in full (1.75 cents up to 2). That is the conservative end; run-features-15m.json uses 100.

params.source: Bounded Oct8-12 native decision features; same frozen W4 GRU.

write.notes: The W4 decision table with fair_gru, the out-of-sample fair_blend and fair_blend_status (warmup rows included, so the whole W4 is auditable), fees and the label, as canonical JSON lines, one file per run. Nothing reads this path until it is published through onboarding. The directory must exist (runbook B8).
